$comment: Advisories consciously accepted by the 🔒 Security Audit gate. Every entry needs a reason and a reviewBy date; check-npm-audit.js fails once an entry expires or stops matching a live advisory, so exceptions cannot rot silently.

allow.title: extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal
allow.reason: No patched release exists — the advisory covers extract-zip at range '*', and 2.0.1 is still the latest published version. It reaches us only as a transitive devDependency of the two browser-driving test tools: @lhci/cli 0.15.1 -> lighthouse 12.6.1 -> puppeteer-core 24.x -> @puppeteer/browsers 2.x, and pa11y-ci 4.1.1 -> puppeteer -> @puppeteer/browsers 2.x. Both tools are already at their latest published versions and @lhci/cli 0.15.1 hard-pins lighthouse to exactly 12.6.1, so there is no forward upgrade available to us; npm's own remedy is a downgrade to lighthouse 10.1.1 and pa11y-ci 3.1.0, multiple majors back, which would break the performance and accessibility gates. The fix exists upstream — @puppeteer/browsers 3.2.0 replaced extract-zip with modern-tar, and lighthouse 13.4.1 already consumes it — so this entry should be removed as soon as @lhci/cli picks up lighthouse 13.x. Exposure is limited to CI: package.json declares zero runtime dependencies, so none of this ships to readers, and the only archives these packages extract are Chrome builds fetched from Google's official download endpoints during test setup, not attacker-supplied zips.
